newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA says seeks delay in new U.S. overflight fees.
newsitem.headline: IATA says seeks delay in new U.S. overflight fees.

text.p: The global airlines body IATA said on Monday it has asked the United States to delay the introduction of overflight fees due to go into effect on May 19 for planes crossing through U.S. airspace.

IATA, the International Air Transport Association, said it had taken the action on behalf of 75 member-carriers who fly routes across the United States which do not involve landing or takeoff at U.S. airports.

The Geneva- and Montreal-based body said in a statement it did not challenge the United States's right to introduce "fair and reasonable charges" for the use of air navigation facilities and services in U.S. airspace.
But it was concerned at what it called "the absence of meaningful consultation" between the U.S. Department of Transportation and the affected airlines.

In a letter to Transport Secretary Rodney Slater quoted in the statement, IATA Director-General Pierre Jeanniot said consultations "should provide complete transparency of information about the costs of providing overflight services and the methods used to allocate those costs to the various categories of users".
Jeanniot said IATA was asking Washington to "adhere to standard international practice".

"Consultation with users in advance of the introduction of new charges is no more than the United States government and U.S. flag carriers demand when a foreign charging authority plans to introduce new charges of this magnitude," he added,
